findings.state: Manual sender action between preview and execution
findings.title: Published Gmail recheck guarantee is stronger than the worker implementation

evidence.detail: Canonical action-preview copy says DeclutrMail checks Gmail again when the action runs.
Terms specifically says the worker re-checks Gmail at execution.
Machine-readable pricing repeats the execution-time Gmail check.
Static public summary repeats the same guarantee.
Sender selector is resolved again by resolveSenderActionIds.
resolveSenderActionIds selects provider IDs from the local mailMessages database using senderActionWhere; it does not fetch current Gmail scope.
The resolved local IDs are passed directly to Gmail batchModify.
batchModify only posts the supplied IDs and label changes in chunks; it performs no Gmail message-scope read.

findings.recommendation: Remove the claim that Gmail is rechecked. Describe that the matching scope is resolved again when execution starts and the final count can differ, or implement and verify an actual provider recheck before retaining the guarantee. Keep the current-index wording in the Delete guide; that wording matches the implementation.
findings.verification: Source trace from selector resolution through Gmail mutation adapter; no provider mutation or production freshness test performed. A Gmail label-name lookup is not a current message-scope recheck.
findings.launchImpact: A user may approve a preview believing the provider is freshly checked. This trust guarantee should match the implementation before launch.

Visible guide correctly says Keep is inline and affected-email previews apply to mail-moving actions.

The live affected-email preview gate covers Archive, Later, Delete, and Unsubscribe only when historic Archive is selected.
Canonical recovery claim includes Activity Undo for Delete.

findings.recommendation: Align JSON-LD and pricing markdown with the visible guide: Keep records an inline decision; mail-moving actions show the affected-email preview; unsubscribe confirms its method and any optional separate cleanup. Include Delete with Archive/Later when listing Activity Undo.

findings.state: Keyboard Help or another dialog open over focus card
findings.title: Triage decision shortcuts remain active behind modal dialogs

actionsDisabled is only busy or inlinePreviewGates.blocked; Keyboard Help/dialog state does not disable it.

findings.state: Custom return time while device timezone differs from account preference
findings.title: Custom Later time uses device timezone while the screen and presets use account timezone

findings.recommendation: Interpret the custom wall time in the same explicit account zone as presets/rows, or clearly name and consistently display the device zone. Preview the resolved return time before saving, including DST handling.
findings.verification: Source plus pure runtime demonstration: with device TZ=UTC/account America/Los_Angeles, entering 2026-10-04T09:00 serializes 09:00Z and renders back as 2:00 AM Los Angeles, seven hours earlier than the apparent 9:00 AM choice. findings.launchImpact: Traveling users or users with a different saved timezone can return mail at the wrong hour.

findings.state: URL filter transition with placeholder rows retained

findings.route: root/global errors, core route errors and account menu
findings.state: Render failure or ambiguous mutation failure
findings.title: Error copy asserts untouched state and automatic background recovery without outcome evidence

evidence.detail: Root error promises mailbox/decisions untouched and retry the rest in the background, but only passes reset/escape to RouteErrorScreen.
Boundary only captures diagnostics and exposes manual reset/escape; it does not reconcile mutation outcome or schedule background retry.
Global heading says DeclutrMail is reloading although reload begins only on the explicit reset button.
Global failure likewise promises untouched mailbox/decisions without reading persisted/provider state.
Keep onError says nothing changed; request failure can be an ambiguous response after server commit.
Indexed-data deletion onError says Nothing was deleted even though it only knows the request failed client-side.
Deletion endpoint disconnects first, then durably queues deletion, before returning its response; lost response cannot prove no write.

findings.recommendation: Delete unverifiable assurances and automatic-retry promises. State only what could not be loaded or confirmed, give one next step, and reconcile ambiguous write outcomes before claiming no change. Keep factual Gmail safety statements only when the operation contract proves them.
findings.verification: Root AppError default browser fixture displayed the exact assurance/background-retry copy. Global behavior and ambiguous-write examples are source-only; no crashes, deletions or Keep writes induced. Parent-reported blank GlobalError fixture is a coverage gap.404 is not blanket included.
findings.launchImpact: A user can be told nothing changed after a decision or durable deletion actually started, or wait for recovery that was never scheduled.

findings.launchImpact: Lower priority for consumer marketing, but impairs operator access to launch diagnostics.

findings.state: Dark-theme danger and protected-warning text

findings.recommendation: Provide a stronger text-danger token for soft/tinted surfaces and remove opacity from meaningful confidence labels where it breaks contrast. Verify each rendered background rather than changing only one button.
findings.verification: Browser axe measured Triage Delete 3.18:1; sender detail Delete 3.44:1; Screener pressed Delete 3.28:1 and Protected warning 3.09:1; Activity Review 4.20:1; Screener unsure 4.25:1. These small text instances need 4.5:1. Disabled controls were not used as evidence.
findings.launchImpact: Destructive choices and protection warnings need especially clear legibility.
